# May Institute Essentials 2026

> May Institute Essentials is a condensed, fully virtual version of the May
> Institute, covering computation and statistics for mass spectrometry-based
> proteomics. It runs November 2-6, 2026, online. Sessions are led by the
> developers of the methods and software they teach.

Site: https://vitek-lab.github.io/MIe-2026/

## Program at a glance

- Dates: November 2-6, 2026 (Monday through Friday)
- Time: 10:00 a.m. - 12:30 p.m. EST each day (7:00-9:30 a.m. PST, 4:00-6:30 p.m. CET)
- Format: fully online; five sessions, one per day
- Audience: early career researchers and established scientists in experimental
  or computational proteomics
- Cost: $50 academic, non-profit, and governmental; $100 commercial. A single
  fee covers the full week.
- Registration: not yet open as of this writing. The registration link will
  appear at https://vitek-lab.github.io/MIe-2026/#register
- Contact: mayinstitute@northeastern.edu
- Host: May Institute, Barnett Institute and Khoury College of Computer
  Sciences, Northeastern University

Registration includes access to all sessions, interactive discussion with
presenters, 1:1 office hours with the tool developers, presentation materials
(slides, code, datasets), and early access to recordings.

## Courses

Days 1-3 cover MSstats; days 4-5 cover Cardinal.

- [MSstats: statistics for mass spectrometry proteomics](https://vitek-lab.github.io/MIe-2026/msstats.html):
  November 2-4, 2026. Statistical analysis of quantitative MS-based proteomic
  experiments with MSstats: normalization, missing value imputation,
  summarization of protein abundances, confidence intervals for fold changes,
  testing for differential abundance, and multivariate analysis for biomarker
  discovery. Day 3 covers biological interpretation with MSstatsBioNet and
  INDRA. Taught by Devon Kohler, Sarah Szvetecz, Tony Wu, and Benjamin Gyori.
  Assumes some prior experience with statistics and proteomics.
- [Cardinal: analysis of mass spectrometry imaging data](https://vitek-lab.github.io/MIe-2026/cardinal.html):
  November 5-6, 2026. Data manipulation, visualization, and statistical
  analysis of mass spectrometry imaging (MSI) experiments using Cardinal and R:
  the .imzML format and larger-than-memory datasets, preprocessing
  (recalibration, peak picking, peak alignment, normalization), visualization of
  spectra and ion images, then segmentation, classification, and hypothesis
  testing. Taught by Kylie Bemis, Sai Srikanth Lakkimsetty, Ethan Rogers, and
  Yinyue Zhu. Assumes basic familiarity with R.
